title: EU imposes duties of up to 27.9% on cold-rolled steel from India, Japan and three others
intro: Brussels dominates today's edition. Several publishers report that the European Union has imposed anti-dumping duties on cold-rolled flat steel from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkiye and Vietnam. GMK Center and IndexBox put the top rate at up to 27.9%, and a Korean outlet reports a 16% rate on Vietnamese material. The Commission is also reported to be proposing an extension of its carbon border mechanism to downstream products. In China, BigMint reports iron ore near a four-year low as weak steel prices curb mill buying. In the United States, Nippon Steel is reported to be reviving a Pennsylvania mill and Nucor to be setting shipment records. Most reports today arrived as headlines only, and we note where detail is missing.

marketOverview: Price signals today are directional rather than numerical. BigMint reports that iron ore prices in China have fallen to a near four-year low as weak steel prices curb mill purchasing, and a StoneX headline says China's steel slump has left iron ore bulls under pressure. Neither excerpt gives price levels. In Europe, Shanghai Metals Market reports that hot-rolled coil is holding at highs, again without figures. In the United States, GMK Center reports that Nucor has once more raised its hot-rolled coil price by $15/t, but it does not state the resulting level. The material contains no benchmark price data.

analysis: Analysis: Taken together, today's reports suggest that Europe is tightening its trade defences on two fronts at once. One front is conventional anti-dumping duties on cold-rolled steel; the other is a proposed CBAM extension reaching 180 downstream products. If confirmed, the second could matter more over time, because it would address the risk that carbon costs are avoided by importing finished goods rather than steel. For exporters in India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkiye and Vietnam, the cold-rolled duties could redirect volumes towards other markets at a time when, on BigMint's and StoneX's reporting, Chinese steel demand and iron ore prices are weak. The reported contrast between Europe and America is also notable. European HRC is said to be holding at highs, and Nucor is lifting prices and shipments behind Section 232. Protected regional markets appear to be supporting domestic mills. Meanwhile, POSCO's reported customer agreements and HBI review, alongside Voestalpine's green build, point to producers positioning for a lower-carbon supply chain. Readers should note that most of this material consists of headlines without supporting detail.
